model.name: claude-opus-5[1m]
model.note: Model identity is the actual runtime model of the evaluating session, taken from the session environment (claude-opus-5[1m], Opus 5 with 1M context), not the agent definition's template text, which names claude-fable-5.

issues_detected.description: human_subject_research is entirely absent from a record whose description, instances, subpopulations and sensitive_elements all state that the content is patient-level hospital records for critically ill patients in adult, pediatric and neonatal intensive care units. The top-level source_caveats discloses the omission ('No source states whether the dataset is governed as human subjects research'), so the gap is declared rather than hidden, but a reader is left with no determination either way for a dataset built from identifiable clinical records at 14 hospitals.
issues_detected.recommendation: Record the human subjects determination explicitly, including a 'not human subjects research' or 'exempt secondary use' finding if that is what applies, so the absence reads as a determination rather than as unexamined.

issues_detected.description: No informed_consent slot exists and no consent basis of any kind is asserted. direct_collection.is_direct=false explains coherently that data are extracted retrospectively from records already held by contributing hospitals rather than gathered from individuals, which is a valid reason for the absence of prospective consent, but no waiver of consent, HIPAA authorization waiver, or opt-out route replaces it. The legal basis for secondary use of these records is undocumented.
issues_detected.recommendation: State the consent basis even where it is a waiver, and name the body that granted it, so that a retrospective dataset shows a documented determination rather than a silence.

issues_detected.description: at_risk_populations is left unpopulated while the record's own composition slots identify the vulnerable groups plainly: instances[0] covers admissions to pediatric and neonatal intensive care units, subpopulations[0] names PICU and NICU as identifying settings, and the description repeats both. The source_caveats justifies the omission on the grounds that no source describes protections, assent or guardian consent, but the population itself is identified elsewhere in the same record, so the slot that should carry protections for children and neonates is empty while the slot that names them is full.
issues_detected.recommendation: Populate at_risk_populations with the groups the record already identifies (pediatric and neonatal ICU admissions, critically ill adults unable to consent at the point of care) and record the absence of documented protections as a caveat inside that slot rather than by leaving it empty.

issues_detected.description: No known_biases slot is present. known_limitations[2] carries limitation_type representativeness_limitation and describes a 14-hospital contributing network inside a 20-centre academic collaboration covering ICU, PICU and NICU only, which is a textbook selection bias, and it even names a mitigation. The substance of a bias entry is therefore present but is filed as a limitation and carries no enumerated bias type, so nothing in the record is machine-readable as bias categorization.
issues_detected.recommendation: Register the representativeness finding under known_biases with a BiasTypeEnum value (selection_bias) and keep the mitigation_strategy already written, so the RAI-aligned taxonomy is populated rather than implied by prose in another slot.

issues_detected.description: No persistent identifier exists. id is 'https://chorus4ai.org/#chorus-dataset', a fragment appended to the project homepage, and page is the same homepage. There is no DOI, no RRID, no repository accession, no version and no citation, so there is no DOI prefix or RRID pattern available to validate and nothing supports stable cross-referencing of the released state of the data.
issues_detected.recommendation: Mint a DOI for the released dataset or record the enclave accession approved users are issued, and add a recommended citation so an analysis can name what it read.

issues_detected.description: is_tabular is set to false for a dataset whose largest single component is 1.6 billion rows of structured electronic health record data standardized to the OMOP Common Data Model, an explicitly tabular representation. The value is defensible for the multimodal whole, which also holds DICOM, WFDB, EDF+ and tokenized text, but it is a single coarse flag over heterogeneous content and there is no variables slot to carry the structured portion's shape, so the one field that speaks to tabular structure denies it.
issues_detected.recommendation: Either qualify the flag in a note stating that the OMOP portion is tabular while other modalities are not, or set it per subset, so the flag is not read as a claim that no tabular data exist.

issues_detected.description: status describes a 'Partial release available under controlled access as of August 2025, with acquisition and modality expansion continuing', and updates describes growth toward an anticipated final dataset, yet no version, version_access, errata or release_notes is recorded. A dataset that the record itself describes as moving from 50,000 toward 100,000 admissions with modalities arriving at different times is versionable by construction, and a reuser cannot name the state of the data they analysed.
issues_detected.recommendation: Assign a version identifier to the August 2025 released state and describe how earlier states can be accessed, or state that the enclave carries a single rolling snapshot with no retrievable history.

issues_detected.description: third_party_sharing.is_shared=true and access is described in operational detail (named contacts, registration form, signed licensing agreement, .edu address requirement, provisioned compute), but no publisher and no download_url is recorded and the data live in a project-operated cloud enclave rather than a recognized repository. The access entry point is reduced to two email addresses inside data_governance.access_review_process prose, which cannot be resolved or bookmarked.
issues_detected.recommendation: Name the hosting platform of record and give a resolvable access-request URL in place of email addresses in prose.

issues_detected.description: ethical_reviews.reviewing_organization asserts 'CHoRUS consortium ethics pillar' while the same entry's source_caveats states that no source names an institutional review board, ethics committee approval, or protocol number. A project workstream that runs community focus groups and analyzes the legal landscape is not a reviewing body for this dataset, so the structured field claims a reviewer that the caveat immediately disclaims.
issues_detected.recommendation: Leave reviewing_organization unset when no reviewing body is named in the sources, and keep the ethics pillar description in review_details where it belongs, so a structured field is not read as an approval chain.

issues_detected.description: is_deidentified describes methods (OHNLP tokenization, imaging de-identification, transformations limiting re-identification) and its source_caveats concedes that no source states which identifier categories are removed nor quantifies residual risk. participant_privacy then documents anonymization_method, privacy_techniques and data_linkage but carries no reidentification_risk field at all. The record is candid, but a dataset holding waveform telemetry, imaging and geocoded OMOP Location entities has an unaddressed re-identification profile and the linkage disclosure in the same slot makes that profile visible without assessing it.
issues_detected.recommendation: Add a residual re-identification risk determination naming its level, the method used to reach it and the party responsible, or state plainly that no assessment has been performed, given that the record discloses cross-modality linkage at admission level and geocoding.

issues_detected.description: Two address defects are transcribed from the sources and labelled rather than silently repaired: the program manager address 'cmccrary@mgh.havard.edu' carries a misspelled domain and is marked '(as published)' in both maintainers and data_governance.stewardship_roles, and the external resource 'www.bridge2ai.org/chorus' is recorded without a scheme so it is not resolvable as written. The website banner quoted in notes preserves the source's own misspelling of 'repoitory' with an explicit '(spelling as published)' marker.
issues_detected.recommendation: Keep the caveated transcription of the misspelled address but normalize the schemeless host to https:// so the external resource resolves.

issues_detected.description: Ontology CURIEs are syntactically well formed and use the Bridge2AI prefixes (data_topic B2AI_TOPIC:4, :6, :7, :8, :9, :15, :32, :37 and data_substrate B2AI_SUBSTRATE:11, :43, :49 across eleven instances entries), but B2AI_TOPIC:4 is assigned to three semantically distinct instance types (patient admission, provider-documented procedure record, and nursing flowsheet entry). Either the term is broad enough to cover all three or one assignment is imprecise, and the referents cannot be resolved offline to tell which.
issues_detected.recommendation: Carry the human-readable label of each ontology term beside the CURIE so a reader can see whether one code legitimately spans admissions, procedures and flowsheet entries.

semantic_insights: The description is quantified and modality-resolved rather than promotional: 50,000 released patient admissions across adult, pediatric and neonatal ICUs, 1.6 billion OMOP rows, 7,642 admissions with radiology data, 23 Tb of waveform data, 14 contributing hospitals inside a 20-centre collaboration of more than 60 members, and every figure it states reappears in a structured slot.

Released and anticipated are held apart consistently. The 50,000-admission release is distinguished from the 100,000-admission anticipated dataset in description, instances notes, known_limitations and updates, and the holdout test set is recorded under splits as provisioned rather than as a partition already present in the data.

The top-level source_caveats is a genuine reconciliation rather than boilerplate. It names the 50,000 versus 45,000 admission divergence between the project documentation and the September 2025 webinar, states which source was ranked higher and why the other figure is retained, distinguishes project-level from dataset-level statements in the bundle, and enumerates precisely what the bundle does not contain (version, DOI, citation, release date, retention policy, errata, registry identifiers).

Grant documentation is exemplary and passes format validation. OT2OD032701 with project number 1OT2OD032701-01, NIH application ID 10472824, the fiscal-year 2022 award amount, the awardee institution and the 2022-09-01 to 2026-11-30 project period, plus the resolvable RePORTER URL. OT2 is a valid Other Transaction mechanism and OD is the correct Office of the Director code for a Common Fund Bridge2AI data generation award.

The MIT licence is correctly scoped. license_and_use_terms.notes places MIT and Apache-2.0 on the chorus-ai code repositories and states that these terms govern CHoRUS software rather than the dataset, while license_terms carries the separate signed licensing agreement route. A record that read the GitHub licence as the dataset licence would have been materially wrong about reuse rights.

The enclave architecture is documented as a privacy mechanism, not merely as infrastructure. Clinical notes stay at contributing sites with only OHNLP tokens transferred, and the same fact appears coherently in description, is_deidentified, participant_privacy, raw_data_sources, collection_mechanisms, preprocessing_strategies, confidential_elements and known_limitations without drift.

The processing chain names its implementing repository at every step: chorus-mapping for validated semantic mappings, chorus_waveform and chorus_waveform_resources for waveform conversion, chorus-extract-upload and Chorus_SOP for site extracts, CHoRUSReports for characterization reports returned to sites, UF-Geocoding and DeGauss for geocoding OMOP Location entities. Another site could in principle follow the same path.

cleaning_strategies documents a real feedback loop rather than a quality claim: characterization reports are produced and returned to each contributing site after every submission, and semantic mappings undergo clinical validation by clinical collaborators under a named SOP before use.

labeling_strategies and machine_annotation_tools are both populated, with the OHNLP toolkit tied to note tokenization and its output schema, and UF-Geocoding tied to DeGauss geocoding. Naming the annotation tooling separately from preprocessing is a distinction many records of this dataset omit.

known_limitations uses the enumerated limitation_type vocabulary across four entries (coverage, integration, representativeness, scope) and three of the four state a consequence for analysis rather than only a shortfall, for example that local retention of note text means full note text cannot be analysed centrally alongside the other modalities.

regulatory_restrictions.confidentiality_level is set to the enumerated value 'restricted', which is a real sensitivity classification rather than prose, and it agrees with the controlled-access statements carried in confidential_elements, distribution_formats and license_and_use_terms.

The governance compromise is disclosed rather than hidden: data_governance.source_caveats states that Massachusetts General Hospital is recorded as accountable because it is the awardee institution and hosts the program manager, that no source names a formal data access committee, and that Jared Houghtaling is recorded as committee contact only because he is one of two named access-request addresses, the other being an unnamed email. The reader can see exactly how much of that block is inference.

correctness_validations.url_validity: mostly_valid (https://chorus4ai.org/, https://github.com/chorus-ai and https://reporter.nih.gov/project-details/10472824 are well formed and resolvable; 'www.bridge2ai.org/chorus' is recorded without a scheme; the contact address 'cmccrary@mgh.havard.edu' carries a misspelled domain, transcribed as published and marked as such)

elements.name: Dataset Discovery and Identification
elements.description: Can a user or system discover and uniquely identify this dataset?

sub_elements.name: Persistent Identifier (DOI, RRID, or URI)
sub_elements.evidence: id: 'https://chorus4ai.org/#chorus-dataset'; no doi, no rrid, no repository accession, no citation and no version anywhere in the record. The top-level source_caveats states that 'No version identifier, DOI, citation, release date, retention policy, or errata for the dataset appear anywhere in the bundle'
sub_elements.quality_note: The identifier is a fragment appended to the project homepage. That distinguishes the dataset from the site within this record but carries no registration, resolves to a living page whose content changes as the project grows toward the 100,000-admission target, and pins no version. There is no DOI prefix or RRID pattern available to validate.

sub_elements.name: Dataset Title and Description Completeness
sub_elements.evidence: title: 'Patient-Focused Collaborative Hospital Repository Uniting Standards (CHoRUS) for Equitable AI'; name: 'CHoRUS dataset'; description of roughly 1,600 characters covering the Bridge2AI programme context, 14 contributing hospitals within a 20-centre collaboration of more than 60 members, 50,000 released admissions across adult, pediatric and neonatal ICUs, 1.6 billion OMOP rows, 7,642 admissions with radiology, 23 Tb of waveform data, the anticipated 100,000-admission target across nine modalities, per-modality standards (OMOP, OHNLP, DICOM, WFDB, EDF+/Persyst), the controlled-access enclave with notes retained on site, and the planned sequestered holdout set
sub_elements.quality_note: Both the full programme title and the short citable name exist. The description is quantified, modality-resolved and semantically appropriate for a multicenter critical care dataset, and it separates released from anticipated figures inline so a reader is not misled about what is obtainable.

sub_elements.name: Keywords or Tags for Searchability
sub_elements.evidence: keywords: 14 entries including 'critical care', 'acute illness', 'intensive care unit', 'electronic health record', 'OMOP Common Data Model', 'physiologic waveforms', 'electroencephalography', 'medical imaging', 'clinical notes', 'social determinants of health', 'AI-ready dataset', 'Bridge2AI', 'multimodal data', 'controlled access'
sub_elements.quality_note: Well above the five-keyword threshold and genuinely discriminating rather than padded. Clinical domain, care setting, every modality, the data model, the access regime and the funding programme are all indexable, and each term is one a critical care AI researcher would plausibly search on.

sub_elements.name: Landing Page and Resources (page, hierarchical resources)
sub_elements.evidence: page: 'https://chorus4ai.org/'; external_resources: five entries covering the project website with its page inventory (team, project overview, tools, data acquisition, standards, community engagement, ethics, the dataset, learning resources), the chorus-ai GitHub organization, the NIH RePORTER award record, the Bridge2AI CHoRUS programme page and the September 2025 training webinar; instances decomposes the dataset into eleven typed entries by modality and content type
sub_elements.quality_note: A well-formed landing page plus a real internal decomposition by modality through instances, each carrying its own topic and substrate coding and access note. There is no subsets or resources slot, so the hierarchy is expressed through instances rather than through typed dataset components, which is the weaker of the two available structures but still lets a reuser navigate the content modality by modality.

sub_elements.name: Hierarchical Structure (parent datasets, relationships)
sub_elements.evidence: No parent_datasets and no related_datasets. purposes[2] names CHoRUS as 'one of four data generation projects in the NIH-funded Bridge2AI consortium' and external_resources links the Bridge2AI CHoRUS programme page, but no dataset is identified and no relationship is typed
sub_elements.quality_note: The sibling relationships exist and the record states them in prose, yet no dataset-to-dataset link is expressed in a structured slot. raw_data_sources describes the originating hospital systems rather than a parent dataset, so neither external lineage nor consortium relationships are machine-readable.

elements.name: Dataset Access and Retrieval
elements.description: Can the dataset and its associated resources be located, accessed, and downloaded?

sub_elements.name: Access Policy and IP Restrictions Defined
sub_elements.evidence: license_and_use_terms.license_terms: 'All data types are made available under controlled access only. Users of the dataset through the AIM-AHEAD Bridge2AI for Clinical Care Training Program must sign a licensing agreement included in the registration form before gaining access to the dataset, and must have a ".edu" email address to gain access'; notes scoping MIT and Apache-2.0 to the chorus-ai repositories 'rather than the dataset'; data_governance.access_review_process naming the two request addresses and the registration route
sub_elements.quality_note: The access policy is operational rather than nominal: a reader learns what they must sign, what address domain they need, who to write to and that compute is provisioned once access is granted. The explicit separation of the software licences from the dataset terms forestalls the most likely misreading of this record, and the contact_person caveat states that no licensing-specific contact is named in the sources.

sub_elements.name: Regulatory Restrictions and Confidentiality Level Specified
sub_elements.evidence: regulatory_restrictions.confidentiality_level: 'restricted'; regulatory_restrictions.regulatory_restrictions[0]: 'The project established a legal framework for collecting data at scale and analyzes the existing legal and regulatory landscape to manage privacy and bias; all data types are distributed under controlled access only'
sub_elements.quality_note: A sensitivity classification is set with an enumerated value and it agrees with the controlled-access statements carried in confidential_elements, distribution_formats and license_and_use_terms, so a reuser knows the handling class before requesting access. The regulatory half is thin: a legal framework and a landscape analysis are named but no framework is identified, and HIPAA is never mentioned for a US multi-site dataset built from identifiable EHR, imaging and clinical notes.

sub_elements.name: Download URL or Platform Link Available
sub_elements.evidence: No download_url. data_governance.access_review_process: 'Access is requested from the named CHoRUS contacts (dbold@emory.edu or jared.houghtaling@tuftsmedicine.org)', with the AIM-AHEAD registration form as the alternative route and provisioning notified by email
sub_elements.quality_note: The route to access is described but no link is given, not even a request form URL. A direct download link would be inappropriate for data held in a provisioned enclave, but the entry point is reduced to two email addresses in prose, which cannot be resolved, bookmarked or checked for currency.

sub_elements.name: Distribution Formats and File Types Specified
sub_elements.evidence: distribution_formats: five entries, OMOP Common Data Model tables for the structured EHR content, OHNLP toolkit output for tokenized notes, DICOM for PACS imaging, WFDB for waveform telemetry and 'EDF+ and Persyst' for EEG, each with a note recording the access condition and the published metadata schema
sub_elements.quality_note: Formats are specific and modality-correct, and they agree with raw_data_sources, conforms_to and the instances entries without drift. The record is loose in one respect: OMOP and OHNLP are data standards rather than delivery formats and are presented here as formats without the distinction being drawn. No media types, file extensions or packaging are given.

sub_elements.name: Related Datasets and External Resources Linked
sub_elements.evidence: external_resources: five entries, the CHoRUS project website with its page inventory, the chorus-ai GitHub organization hosting software, validated semantic mappings, SOPs and project boards, the NIH RePORTER record for OT2OD032701, the Bridge2AI CHoRUS programme page and the September 2025 AIM-AHEAD training webinar
sub_elements.quality_note: Each resource is described by what a reader will find there rather than by title alone, and the set spans documentation, code, funding provenance and outreach. related_datasets is absent and one URL is schemeless, but the external documentation half of this sub-element is well served.

elements.name: Data Reuse and Interoperability
elements.description: Is sufficient information provided to reuse and integrate the dataset with others?

sub_elements.name: License Terms Allow Reuse
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: Shared condition met via E2 fields: distribution_formats lists five formats, third_party_sharing.is_shared=true stating the dataset 'is made available to approved external users under controlled access through a cloud enclave', and license_and_use_terms describes a signed-agreement route to access. Under the ambiguity rule, controlled access with a documented approval route is scored rather than excluded
sub_elements.evidence: license_and_use_terms.license_terms describes controlled access and a signed licensing agreement but names no licence for the data; notes place MIT and Apache-2.0 on the chorus-ai repositories and state that 'these terms govern CHoRUS software rather than the dataset'
sub_elements.quality_note: No reuse licence exists for the dataset itself. A reader learns how to obtain access but not what may be done with the data afterwards: no CC or ODC identifier, no redistribution or publication terms, no attribution requirement, and the agreement's content is never summarized. The record is accurate that the gap lies in the sources, but the sub-element asks whether reuse terms permit reuse and they cannot be determined from what is recorded.

sub_elements.name: Data Formats Are Standardized (encoding, format)
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: Same shared condition as above, evidenced by distribution_formats and third_party_sharing in E2
sub_elements.evidence: conforms_to_standard: [OMOP_CDM, DICOM, WFDB, OTHER]; distribution_formats naming OMOP CDM tables, OHNLP output, DICOM, WFDB, and EDF+ with Persyst; raw_data_sources recording the pre-transformation format for each modality
sub_elements.quality_note: Every modality sits on a recognized open standard appropriate to its data type, and the same standard is asserted consistently at the top level, in distribution_formats, in raw_data_sources and in the instances notes with no drift. Persyst is a vendor format and is honestly folded into OTHER rather than overclaimed. Character encoding is never stated, which matters for the tokenized clinical text.

sub_elements.name: Schema or Ontology Conformance Stated
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: Same shared condition as above, evidenced by distribution_formats and third_party_sharing in E2
sub_elements.evidence: conforms_to: prose mapping each content type to its standard, from OMOP for structured clinical data through OMOP-with-extensions for nursing flowsheets, DICOM for imaging, WFDB with the PhysioNet schema extended for telemetry, EDF+ and Persyst for EEG and OHNLP for tokenized notes; conforms_to_schema: 'https://w3id.org/bridge2ai/data-sheets-schema'; conforms_to_class: Dataset; instances carrying B2AI_TOPIC and B2AI_SUBSTRATE CURIEs
sub_elements.quality_note: Conformance is stated at three levels: the data standard governing each modality, the metadata schema this record itself conforms to, and ontology CURIEs on the instance entries. OMOP is the correct interoperability anchor for multi-site EHR and the record binds it to specific content types, including the extension for nursing flowsheets, rather than asserting it globally.

sub_elements.name: Variable Metadata with Identifiers Defined
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: Same shared condition as above, evidenced by distribution_formats and third_party_sharing in E2
sub_elements.evidence: No variables slot. The nearest content is instances enumerating content types (demographics, medication administration with dosing 'time-stamped upon each infusion change or dose administration', procedures, nursing flowsheets, diagnoses) and raw_data_sources[0] describing the same coverage at source-system level
sub_elements.quality_note: Content areas are described but no variable, column, field or concept is defined with an identifier. OMOP conformance points at a published table and concept structure, so a reuser can reach a variable model indirectly, but nothing here names which OMOP tables or concept sets are actually populated, and the imaging, waveform, EEG and note modalities have no variable documentation at all.

sub_elements.name: Use Guidance Provided (intended, prohibited uses)
sub_elements.evidence: intended_uses: three typed categories (clinical AI/ML model development, external model validation, education and workforce development) each with worked examples naming the holdout test set, canonical Jupyter notebooks and OHDSI tool stack workshops; existing_uses recording the AIM-AHEAD cohort 2 training programme starting 17 November 2025 and publications; other_tasks describing downstream analytics and mapping tooling development; tasks listing four analytic objectives
sub_elements.quality_note: Intended use is specific enough to act on, and the use_category values are meaningful rather than restatements of the title. Each category maps onto a capability the dataset actually holds. prohibited_uses and discouraged_uses are both absent, which is a real gap for controlled clinical data where re-identification attempts and out-of-scope inference should be named explicitly.

elements.name: Ethical Use and Privacy Safeguards
elements.description: Does the dataset provide clear information about consent, privacy, and ethical oversight?

sub_elements.name: IRB or Ethics Review and Data Protection Impact
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: Human subjects condition met via E1 fields: description states the dataset 'assembles retrospective, controlled-access clinical data on critically ill patients from 14 data-contributing hospitals' covering adult, pediatric and neonatal ICUs, and keywords include 'critical care', 'intensive care unit', 'electronic health record' and 'clinical notes'. E8 collection_mechanisms independently describes extraction of patient records from hospital EHR, PACS, monitor and EEG systems. Governance condition also met via E2: regulatory_restrictions.confidentiality_level is 'restricted'. E4's own fields are not used as the applicability signal
sub_elements.evidence: ethical_reviews[0].review_details describes the Ethical and Trustworthy AI pillar, community-facing ethics focus groups on what data is appropriate for public sharing, evaluation of community perspectives on clinical care AI, and analysis of the legal and regulatory landscape; reviewing_organization: 'CHoRUS consortium ethics pillar'; source_caveats: 'No source names an institutional review board, ethics committee approval, or protocol number for the dataset'. No data_protection_impacts; data_governance.committee_contact names Jared Houghtaling with its own caveat that no source identifies him as a committee contact
sub_elements.quality_note: Ethics activity is documented but ethics oversight is not. There is no IRB of record, no approval or waiver, no protocol number and no data protection impact assessment for a dataset assembled from identifiable critical care records at 14 hospitals. The reviewing_organization value compounds this by naming a project workstream as a reviewer that the entry's own caveat disclaims. The candour is real; the sub-element is not satisfied.

sub_elements.name: Deidentification Method Described
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: Same human subjects and governance conditions as above, evidenced by E1 description and keywords, E8 collection_mechanisms and E2 confidentiality_level
sub_elements.evidence: is_deidentified.method: 'Tokenization of unstructured electronic health record text using the OHNLP toolkit; de-identification of imaging prior to release; data transformations that limit re-identification'; deidentification_details: 'Clinical notes are retained locally at contributing sites with only tokens transferred to the enclave; imaging de-identification was in process for a cohort larger than the images available as of September 2025. A privacy scan tool for medical records is maintained in the chorus-ai GitHub organization'; source_caveats conceding that no source states which identifier categories are removed
sub_elements.quality_note: The method is per-modality and semantically appropriate: tokenization for free text, de-identification for imaging, and data minimization by keeping identifiable source material at the contributing sites. The layered defence combining de-identification with controlled access is stated rather than implied, the incomplete imaging step is marked as in process, and a concrete instrument (the privacy scan tool) is named. No recognized standard (Safe Harbor, Expert Determination, k-anonymity) is invoked and no verification is reported, which caps the depth.

sub_elements.name: Privacy Protections and Re-identification Risk Assessment
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: Same human subjects and governance conditions as above, evidenced by E1 description and keywords, E8 collection_mechanisms and E2 confidentiality_level
sub_elements.evidence: participant_privacy[0].anonymization_method: tokenization with the OHNLP toolkit and imaging de-identification; privacy_techniques: 'Controlled access to all data types through a cloud enclave, local retention of clinical notes at contributing sites, transformation approaches that limit re-identification, and a privacy scan tool for medical records'; data_linkage: 'Data from 14 hospitals are harmonized to the OMOP Common Data Model and linked across modalities at the admission level; OMOP Location entities are geocoded to derive contextual geographic factors'. No reidentification_risk field anywhere; is_deidentified.source_caveats concedes that no source 'quantifies residual re-identification risk'
sub_elements.quality_note: Protections are substantive and the linkage disclosure is unusually forthright: the record volunteers that modalities are joined at admission level and that location entities are geocoded, which is precisely the profile that raises re-identification exposure. Having surfaced it, the record then carries no risk assessment at all: no residual level, no determination, no method, no responsible party. The honesty of the caveat does not supply the assessment the sub-element asks for.

sub_elements.name: Informed Consent Obtained from Participants
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: Same human subjects and governance conditions as above, evidenced by E1 description and keywords, E8 collection_mechanisms and E2 confidentiality_level
sub_elements.evidence: No informed_consent slot. direct_collection[0].is_direct: false with collection_details: 'Data are obtained retrospectively from records already held by contributing hospitals (EHR systems, PACS, bedside monitor gateways, and hospital EEG databases) rather than gathered from individuals for the purpose of this dataset'. The top-level source_caveats states that no source 'describes protections, assent, or guardian consent'
sub_elements.quality_note: The record explains why prospective consent does not apply but records nothing in its place: no waiver of consent, no HIPAA authorization waiver, no opt-out mechanism and no withdrawal route. A consortium of this scale that established a legal framework for multi-site collection will have a consent determination somewhere, and none of it reaches the record, so the basis for secondary use of identifiable clinical records is absent alongside the missing IRB.

sub_elements.name: Vulnerable Populations and Compensation Documented
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: Same human subjects and governance conditions as above, evidenced by E1 description and keywords, E8 collection_mechanisms and E2 confidentiality_level
sub_elements.evidence: No at_risk_populations and no participant_compensation. The vulnerable groups are named only in composition slots: instances[0] covers 'adult ICU, pediatric ICU, or neonatal ICU' admissions and subpopulations[0] identifies ICU, PICU and NICU as the identifying settings. The top-level source_caveats states that at_risk_populations is 'left unpopulated' because no source describes protections, assent or guardian consent
sub_elements.quality_note: The record identifies pediatric and neonatal intensive care admissions in its own composition slots and then leaves the slot that should carry protections for them empty. Children, neonates and critically ill adults unable to consent at the point of care are the textbook at-risk groups for this data type, and the population is known to the record even where the protections are not, so the omission of the identification itself is a documentation choice rather than a source limitation. Absent compensation is correct for a retrospective dataset with no participant contact.

elements.name: Data Composition and Structure
elements.description: Can the dataset's structure, modality, and population be understood from metadata?

sub_elements.name: Cohort or Subpopulations Characteristics Described
sub_elements.evidence: subpopulations: two entries with subpopulation_elements_present: true, the first identifying admissions by care setting (adult ICU, PICU, NICU) with distribution stating that the sources report 50,000 released admissions 'without a per-unit breakdown', the second distinguishing admissions by contributing hospital across 14 sites within a 20-centre collaboration
sub_elements.quality_note: Only care-unit type and contributing site are given. No age, sex, race, ethnicity or geographic distribution, no inclusion or exclusion criteria, and no counts against the 50,000 released admissions for any subgroup. A demographics content type is listed under instances and never characterized, so a reuser cannot judge who is in the cohort or whether it suits their question, which is what this sub-element exists to answer.

sub_elements.name: Number of Instances or Samples Reported
sub_elements.evidence: instances: counts of 50,000 patient admissions and 1,600,000,000 rows of OMOP structured data, 7,642 admissions with radiology imaging, and a waveform entry recording 23 Tb; splits describing the sequestered holdout test set provisioned for external validation; instances[0].source_caveats reconciling the 50,000 figure from project documentation against the webinar's 'over 45K unique admissions'
sub_elements.quality_note: Counts are specific, unit-labelled and tied to the released rather than the anticipated dataset, with the competing webinar figure reconciled in place rather than silently dropped. The two source values are both recorded with a stated ranking rationale. The waveform entry carries a data volume in terabytes but no recording or patient count, and the EEG and note modalities carry no counts at all.

sub_elements.name: Variable-Level Metadata and Tabular Flag
sub_elements.evidence: is_tabular: false. No variables slot. The nearest content is instances describing content types and raw_data_sources enumerating source formats
sub_elements.quality_note: The flag is present but no variable, column, field or concept is defined anywhere, and 1.6 billion rows are reported with no statement of what a row contains. The flag's value is also questionable on its own terms: the largest component of the dataset is OMOP-standardized structured data, which is tabular by construction, so a single false for the multimodal whole denies the structure of the part a reuser is most likely to query. OMOP conformance points at an external variable model but does not substitute for one here.

sub_elements.name: Data Topics or Conditions Represented
sub_elements.evidence: instances entries carry data_topic CURIEs B2AI_TOPIC:4, :6, :7, :8, :9, :15, :32 and :37 and data_substrate CURIEs B2AI_SUBSTRATE:11, :43 and :49 across eleven entries; keywords name critical care, acute illness, social determinants of health and every modality; description and instances resolve the coverage into nine content types across ICU, PICU and NICU settings
sub_elements.quality_note: Topics are both ontology-coded and described in prose, and the modality decomposition tells a reuser what kinds of clinical phenomena are represented. The gap is at the condition level: no diagnoses, phenotypes or case mix are enumerated for a dataset whose diagnoses records are one of eleven instance types, so 'critical illness' remains the finest condition granularity available.

sub_elements.name: Data Quality Issues and Anomalies Documented
sub_elements.evidence: sampling_strategies[0].is_sample: true with strategies describing sampling 'designed to ensure comprehensive sets of patient conditions and clinical treatment strategies across contributing sites' and federated access enabling a balanced and diverse cohort, and source_data naming the retrospective clinical records of 14 acquisition centres; known_limitations recording partial imaging coverage with de-identification in process, EEG extraction still in process, and note text held locally so only tokens are centrally available; no anomalies slot
sub_elements.quality_note: The sampling method and the source frame are documented, and three concrete availability gaps are recorded with their causes, so a reuser planning an imaging or NLP study learns the limit before requesting access. It passes on the sampling and missing-data halves rather than across the board: anomalies, outliers and per-field completeness are documented nowhere, and the coverage gaps sit under known_limitations rather than in a composition slot.

elements.name: Data Provenance and Version Tracking
elements.description: Can a user determine dataset versions, update history, and provenance?

sub_elements.name: Dataset Version Number Provided
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: Shared condition met via E2 fields: distribution_formats populated across five formats and third_party_sharing.is_shared=true describing availability to approved external users through a cloud enclave
sub_elements.evidence: No version. status: 'Partial release available under controlled access as of August 2025, with acquisition and modality expansion continuing toward the anticipated final dataset'; the top-level source_caveats confirms that no version identifier appears anywhere in the bundle
sub_elements.quality_note: A release state is described in prose and dated to August 2025 but never given an identifier. Since the record itself describes the dataset growing from 50,000 toward 100,000 admissions with modalities arriving at different times, a reuser has no way to name the state of the data they analysed or to tell a later reader which snapshot their results rest on.

sub_elements.name: Version Access Methods Documented
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: Same shared condition as above, evidenced by distribution_formats and third_party_sharing in E2
sub_elements.evidence: No version_access. Nothing in updates, status or data_governance describes how a prior state of the data could be retrieved
sub_elements.quality_note: With no versions there is nothing to access. The enclave model would make snapshot access technically feasible, and the record neither offers it nor states that only a rolling current state exists, so a reuser cannot even establish whether reproducing an earlier analysis is possible.

sub_elements.name: Change Descriptions and Errata Provided
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: Same shared condition as above, evidenced by distribution_formats and third_party_sharing in E2
sub_elements.evidence: No errata and no release_notes; the top-level source_caveats states that none appear in the bundle. updates.update_details describes growth toward the anticipated final dataset with imaging de-identification and EEG extraction in process as of September 2025
sub_elements.quality_note: What is documented is a forward trajectory, not a change history. No correction, retraction or restatement of a previously released figure is recorded, even though the record itself surfaces a 50,000 against 45,000 admission discrepancy between two sources that a change log would have resolved.

sub_elements.name: Update Schedule or Frequency Indicated
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: Same shared condition as above, evidenced by distribution_formats and third_party_sharing in E2
sub_elements.evidence: updates.frequency: 'Ongoing during the project period, with regular status updates from contributing sites'; updates.update_details: 'Data contributing sites provide regular status updates on their progress creating and curating CHoRUS data extracts, submitted through the GitHub interface or a Google Form that triggers updates to GitHub issues and status boards. The released dataset is growing toward an anticipated final dataset of 100,000 patient admissions and nine modalities, with imaging de-identification and EEG extraction in process as of September 2025'; the project period 2022-09-01 to 2026-11-30 is recorded under funders and collection_timeframes
sub_elements.quality_note: A frequency is stated and it is bounded rather than open-ended: continuous updating within a project period the record dates elsewhere, with the update mechanism described operationally and the specific work in flight named. The weakness is that the cadence describes site submission and status reporting rather than release to approved users, so a reuser learns that the data are moving but not when a new state reaches them.

sub_elements.name: Provenance and Source Derivation Documented
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: Same shared condition as above, evidenced by distribution_formats and third_party_sharing in E2
sub_elements.evidence: raw_data_sources: five entries, each with source_description, source_type, raw_data_format and access_details, covering structured EHR held by contributing hospitals mapped to OMOP, unstructured notes tokenized with OHNLP and retained on site, PACS imaging in DICOM with de-identification in process, bedside telemetry in WFDB with the PhysioNet schema extended, and hospital EEG databases in EDF+ and Persyst; acquisition_methods separating retrospective extraction from derived content with was_inferred_derived: true
sub_elements.quality_note: Provenance is traced to the originating clinical system for every modality, with the pre-transformation format and the access condition recorded per source, so the chain from routine care through site extract to harmonized enclave content is followable end to end. was_derived_from and release_notes are absent, so the derivation is expressed through raw_data_sources rather than through a dataset lineage slot.

elements.name: Scientific Motivation and Funding Transparency
elements.description: Does the metadata clearly state why the dataset exists and who funded it?

sub_elements.name: Motivation or Purpose for Dataset Creation
sub_elements.evidence: purposes: four responses covering ML and AI applications characterizing acute and critical care illness, a publicly available AI-ready critical care dataset with privacy, accountability and clinical benefit, ethically sourced datasets and best practices for AI in health across Bridge2AI, and network, tools, standards, data and education to improve outcomes for critical care patients. addressing_gaps: three responses naming the infrastructure gap for AI in critical care, the absence of a sufficiently diverse, high-resolution, ethically sourced AI-ready resource, and the legal, standards and contextual-factor barriers to multi-centre acquisition at scale
sub_elements.quality_note: Purpose and the research gap are stated separately and both are substantive. Each gap is specific enough to be contestable rather than generic, and each maps onto a purpose and onto an activity documented elsewhere in the record, which is what distinguishes real motivation from a mission statement.

sub_elements.name: Primary Research Objectives or Tasks
sub_elements.evidence: tasks: characterizing acute and critical care illness; predicting complications and deterioration among patients with acute or critical illness; measuring treatment response; external validation of AI models against a sequestered holdout test set to aid marketplace adoption for implementation in acute and critical care
sub_elements.quality_note: Four analytic objectives that are recognizable ML task framings for critical care data (phenotyping, prognostic prediction, treatment effect, external validation), each answerable with the modalities the dataset actually holds. The holdout validation objective is consistent with the splits entry, which records the holdout as provisioned rather than as a partition already in hand.

sub_elements.name: Funding Sources and Mechanisms Listed
sub_elements.evidence: funders[0].grantor: 'National Institutes of Health (NIH) Common Fund, Bridge2AI program'
sub_elements.quality_note: The agency and the specific funding programme are both named, and the Common Fund Bridge2AI attribution matches the consortium framing used consistently in description, purposes and intended_uses. The mechanism type is implied by the OT2 award code rather than stated in words, and only one funder is recorded.

sub_elements.name: Grant IDs or Award Numbers Present
sub_elements.evidence: funders[0].grants[0].name: OT2OD032701, with notes: 'Project number 1OT2OD032701-01 (core project number OT2OD032701), NIH application ID 10472824, awarded to Massachusetts General Hospital; award amount 5,880,300 for fiscal year 2022, with a project period running from 2022-09-01 to 2026-11-30. The NIH RePORTER record for the award is at https://reporter.nih.gov/project-details/10472824'
sub_elements.quality_note: The award number passes NIH format validation: OT2 is a valid Other Transaction mechanism, OD is the Office of the Director institute code used for Common Fund awards, and both the six-digit serial and the 1...-01 project-number form are well formed. Application ID, award amount, awardee institution, project period and a resolvable RePORTER URL are all present, which is more than the sub-element asks for and enough to verify the award externally.

sub_elements.name: Creators and Acknowledgements Documented
sub_elements.evidence: creators: an entry naming Eric S. Rosenthal as principal_investigator with a Massachusetts General Hospital affiliation and a note tying him to award OT2OD032701 and application 10472824, and a consortium entry naming the leadership team (Azra Bihorac, Xiaoqian Jiang, Yulia Strekalova and Parisa Rashidi at the University of Florida and UTHealth Houston, Manlik Kwong at Tufts University) with the scale of the collaboration; created_by: the CHoRUS Network consortium; maintainers recording the consortium and the chorus-ai GitHub organization with a named program manager
sub_elements.quality_note: Individual leadership, the collective and the maintaining organization are all recorded with affiliations, and the PI is tied to the award recorded under funding. The creators source_caveats is precise about why the five leadership members are held in prose rather than in the principal_investigator field, and it states that no ORCID or ROR appears anywhere in the bundle, so the absence of registry identifiers is explained rather than merely present.

elements.name: Technical Transparency (Data Collection and Processing)
elements.description: Can data collection and processing steps be replicated or understood?

sub_elements.name: Collection Mechanisms and Settings Described
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: Collection identified (acquisition_methods and collection_mechanisms both populated) and the shared condition met via E2 distribution_formats and third_party_sharing.is_shared=true
sub_elements.evidence: collection_mechanisms: five entries covering EHR extraction into OMOP, note extraction and tokenization with the OHNLP toolkit so that only tokens enter the enclave, imaging obtained from hospital PACS in DICOM, waveform capture from bedside monitors via gateway and middleware systems into WFDB with EEG from hospital EEG databases, and site extract creation and upload through the chorus-extract-upload repository following the interactive Chorus_SOP workflow with dockerized container applications on Azure; collection_timeframes recording retrospective collection reported as of August 2025 within the 2022-09-01 to 2026-11-30 project period; data_collectors naming the 14 acquisition centres, the site data managers and the clinical collaborators with their roles
sub_elements.quality_note: Mechanism, setting, timeframe and the people who operate the process are all documented, and each mechanism names the specific tooling and protocol that governs it. The collection_timeframes source_caveats is careful in a way that matters: it states that the calendar range of the underlying clinical encounters is nowhere given and that the dates recorded are the award period, so a reuser is not misled into reading the project period as the data period.

sub_elements.name: Data Acquisition Methods Listed
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: Same conditions as above: collection identified via acquisition_methods and raw_data_sources, shared condition met via E2
sub_elements.evidence: acquisition_methods: a retrospective extraction entry naming the source systems (EHR, PACS, bedside monitors with gateway or middleware, hospital EEG databases) and a derived entry with was_inferred_derived: true covering note tokenization, OMOP mapping and transformations limiting re-identification; raw_data_sources: five entries naming the source system type, the pre-transformation format and the access condition for each modality
sub_elements.quality_note: Observed and derived content are separated with the correct provenance flag, which is the distinction that matters most for a reuser judging what is measurement and what is computation. The originating instrument or system is named for every modality, and derivation steps such as OMOP mapping and geocoding are disclosed as derivation rather than presented as collected data.

sub_elements.name: Preprocessing, Cleaning, Labeling, and Annotation Quality
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: Software-output condition met via E10 external_resources, which names the chorus-ai GitHub organization at https://github.com/chorus-ai hosting software and tooling, validated semantic mappings, SOPs and project boards. E8's own fields are not used as the applicability signal
sub_elements.evidence: preprocessing_strategies: five entries covering OMOP standardization via validated semantic mappings in chorus-mapping, OHNLP extraction and tokenization so only tokens leave the site, transformations limiting re-identification with imaging de-identified before release, waveform conversion via chorus_waveform with chorus_waveform_resources, and DeGauss geocoding of OMOP Location entities via UF-Geocoding. cleaning_strategies: characterization reports produced from CHoRUSReports and returned to contributing sites after each submission, and clinical validation of semantic mappings under a named SOP with internal review of the SOPs themselves. labeling_strategies: a visualization and annotation environment labelling data with targets important for prediction. machine_annotation_tools: the OHNLP toolkit and UF-Geocoding with descriptions
sub_elements.quality_note: All four halves of this sub-element are populated, which is unusual. The pipeline is followable from site extract through harmonization to enclave content and each step names the repository or protocol that implements it, the cleaning entries describe a real feedback loop rather than a claim of quality, and the annotation tooling is recorded separately with the schema its output conforms to. Labeling is the thinnest part: the annotation environment is described but no label taxonomy, inter-annotator agreement or annotation quality analysis is reported.

sub_elements.name: Software and Tools Documented
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: Same software-output condition as above, evidenced by E10 external_resources naming the chorus-ai code organization
sub_elements.evidence: OHNLP toolkit, UF-Geocoding and DeGauss named in machine_annotation_tools and preprocessing_strategies; chorus-mapping, chorus_waveform, chorus_waveform_resources, CHoRUSReports, chorus-extract-upload, Chorus_SOP, the privacy scan tool and dockerized container applications on Azure named across preprocessing_strategies, cleaning_strategies, collection_mechanisms and is_deidentified; extension_mechanism.contribution_url: https://github.com/chorus-ai ; maintainers recording a package status page that 'lists versions, maintainers, and other package metadata' and the chorus-developer web guide
sub_elements.quality_note: Every tool named in the pipeline is traceable to a single resolvable code organization, and a reader can move from a processing step to the repository that performs it. There is no dedicated software_and_tools slot, so the information is distributed across five sections, and no version, release or commit is pinned for any tool, which limits exact reproducibility to whatever the repositories hold at read time.

sub_elements.name: External Standards and Resources Referenced
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: Shared condition met via E2 distribution_formats and third_party_sharing.is_shared=true
sub_elements.evidence: external_resources: the project website with its page inventory, the chorus-ai GitHub organization with software, mappings, SOPs and project boards, the NIH RePORTER award record, the Bridge2AI CHoRUS programme page and the September 2025 AIM-AHEAD webinar; conforms_to and conforms_to_standard naming the OMOP Common Data Model with extensions, DICOM, WFDB with the PhysioNet schema extended, EDF+, Persyst and the OHNLP open-source schema
sub_elements.quality_note: Standards are named per modality and each is the recognized community standard for that data type, while the external resources give a reader the documentation, the code, the funding record and the outreach material behind the record. No standards document is cited by version or URL, and no peer-reviewed publication is referenced anywhere in the record.

elements.name: Dataset Evaluation and Limitations Disclosure
elements.description: Does the metadata communicate known risks, biases, or dataset limitations?

sub_elements.name: Known Limitations Documented
sub_elements.evidence: known_limitations: four entries using the enumerated limitation_type vocabulary, coverage_limitation (roughly 1000 images available with de-identification in process and EEG extraction still in process) with scope_impact stating that analyses requiring imaging or EEG at scale are constrained, integration_limitation (notes held locally with only tokens in the enclave) with scope_impact that full note text cannot be analysed centrally, representativeness_limitation (14 contributing hospitals within a 20-centre academic network, ICU, PICU and NICU only) with a recommended_mitigation, and scope_limitation (50,000 released against 100,000 anticipated across nine modalities)
sub_elements.quality_note: Limitations are typed with the schema vocabulary and three of the four state the consequence for a reuser rather than only the shortfall. They are also honest about the headline claims: the same record that reports imaging as a modality records that most of it is not yet available, and the same record that reports 50,000 admissions records that this is half the anticipated dataset.

sub_elements.name: Biases Categorized Using Standard Taxonomy (RAI-aligned)
sub_elements.evidence: No known_biases slot. known_limitations[2] carries limitation_type representativeness_limitation describing a cohort drawn from 14 contributing hospitals within a 20-centre academic network covering ICU, PICU and NICU only, with a recommended_mitigation naming comprehensive-condition sampling and federated balanced access. future_use_impacts: two entries on trustworthy AI framing and on community-facing ethics focus groups shaping what is appropriate for public sharing
sub_elements.quality_note: The substance of a selection bias entry is present but is filed as a limitation and carries no enumerated bias type, so nothing in the record is machine-readable as bias categorization and no BiasTypeEnum value exists to align with the taxonomy. The future_use_impacts entries speak to governance of downstream use and to managing privacy and bias in the abstract, but neither names an anticipated social impact of the data's composition. Measurement and representation bias across sites and modalities go unregistered entirely.

sub_elements.name: Data Anomalies and Quality Issues Noted
sub_elements.evidence: No anomalies slot. The nearest content is instances[0].source_caveats and the top-level source_caveats reconciling the 50,000 against 45,000 admission divergence between the project documentation and the webinar, and known_limitations on partial modality coverage
sub_elements.quality_note: What is documented is disagreement between sources and incompleteness of coverage, not anomalies in the data. No outliers, artefacts, sensor dropouts, coding inconsistencies across sites or harmonization failures are recorded, which is a conspicuous silence for waveform telemetry and multi-site OMOP mapping, where such issues are near-certain and materially affect analysis. The record even documents a characterization-report feedback loop under cleaning_strategies whose findings would be the natural source for this slot.

sub_elements.name: Sensitive Content and Warnings Provided
sub_elements.evidence: sensitive_elements: three entries with sensitive_elements_present: true, the first enumerating patient-level demographics, diagnoses, medication administration, procedures, nursing flowsheets, notes, imaging and physiologic waveforms, the second naming social determinants of health and geocoded OMOP Location entities including distance to the nearest hospital, the third stating that unstructured notes carry heightened identifiability risk and are therefore retained at contributing sites; confidential_elements recording that every data type is under controlled access and that community ethics focus groups determine what is appropriate for public sharing
sub_elements.quality_note: Sensitivity is enumerated by content type rather than asserted generally, and the record separates ordinary clinical sensitivity from the two elevated cases: geographic context, which is the strongest re-identification vector it holds, and free text, whose handling it then justifies. No content_warnings slot exists, so nothing addresses distressing content such as death and end-of-life documentation in a critical care corpus.

sub_elements.name: Ethical Review Details Including Conflicts
sub_elements.evidence: ethical_reviews[0].review_details describing Ethical and Trustworthy AI as one of the project's three pillars, community-facing ethics focus groups determining what data is appropriate for public sharing, evaluation of community perspectives on clinical care AI to increase trustworthiness of provenance and privacy, and analysis of the existing legal and regulatory landscape, with source_caveats stating that no institutional review board, ethics committee approval, or protocol number is named for the dataset
sub_elements.quality_note: The ethics workstream is described with enough specificity to know what was actually done and who was consulted, and the caveat states plainly what the sources do not establish rather than inflating a workstream into an approval. The reviewing_organization value is nonetheless an over-assertion of that same workstream as a reviewer. No conflicts of interest are declared for a consortium spanning 20 academic centres with an explicit marketplace-adoption objective, which is exactly where a declaration would matter.

elements.name: Cross-Platform and Community Integration
elements.description: Does the dataset connect to wider data ecosystems, repositories, or standards?

sub_elements.name: Dataset Published on a Recognized Platform
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: Shared condition met via E2 fields: distribution_formats populated across five formats and third_party_sharing.is_shared=true describing availability to approved external users through a cloud enclave
sub_elements.evidence: No publisher. The data are described as held under controlled access 'in a cloud enclave' with notes retained at contributing sites; access is granted through named contacts or through the AIM-AHEAD Bridge2AI for Clinical Care Training Program, whose trainees use the Bridge2AI AI/ML for Clinical Care Network and Collaborative Cloud
sub_elements.quality_note: The dataset is not published on a recognized data repository. No PhysioNet, Dataverse, Zenodo, FAIRhub or institutional repository is named, and the hosting environment is a project-operated enclave whose platform of record is never identified in a structured slot. The Bridge2AI Collaborative Cloud appears only inside a training-programme use example, not as a publication venue.

sub_elements.name: Citation and DOI for Cross-referencing
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: Publication condition not met: no citation slot, and external_resources contains only the project website, the chorus-ai GitHub organization, the NIH RePORTER award record, the Bridge2AI programme page and a training webinar, none of which is a publication reference. An award record and a webinar deck are project documentation, not publications. The top-level source_caveats independently states that no citation appears anywhere in the bundle
sub_elements.evidence: No publication reference and no DOI anywhere in the record
sub_elements.quality_note: Excluded from the denominator: the publication condition is not met via E1 or E10 fields, so this sub-element is not scored and one point is removed from the maximum. The absence of a DOI is nonetheless captured as a correctness issue under Element 1.

sub_elements.name: Community Standards or Schema Conformance
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: Same shared condition as above, evidenced by E2 distribution_formats and third_party_sharing
sub_elements.evidence: conforms_to: OMOP Common Data Model for structured clinical data with extensions for nursing flowsheets, DICOM for imaging, WFDB with the PhysioNet schema extended for telemetry, EDF+ and Persyst for EEG, and the OHNLP open-source schema for tokenized notes; conforms_to_standard: [OMOP_CDM, DICOM, WFDB, OTHER]; conforms_to_schema: https://w3id.org/bridge2ai/data-sheets-schema with conforms_to_class: Dataset
sub_elements.quality_note: Every modality is bound to the community standard the relevant research community actually uses, and the metadata record declares its own schema and class as well. The commitment is credible because the same standards recur without drift in distribution_formats, raw_data_sources and the instances notes, and because preprocessing documents the validated semantic mapping work that makes OMOP conformance real rather than asserted.

sub_elements.name: Outreach Materials and Documentation Links
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: Same shared condition as above, evidenced by E2 distribution_formats and third_party_sharing
sub_elements.evidence: external_resources describing the project website's pages on team, project overview, tools, data acquisition, standards, community engagement, ethics, the dataset and learning resources, the GitHub organization's SOPs and mappings, and the September 2025 AIM-AHEAD informational webinar; extension_mechanism.contribution_url: https://github.com/chorus-ai with the Chorus_SOP workflow, the Standards and Data Acquisition discussion spaces and a central GitHub project board; maintainers naming the chorus-developer web guide for contributors and users; intended_uses and existing_uses recording the training programme with its cohort 2 start date of 17 November 2025 and canonical Jupyter notebooks and OHDSI workshops
sub_elements.quality_note: Documentation, contributor guidance, a developer guide and a dated training programme are all recorded, and the routes are concrete: a would-be contributor is told which repository and which discussion board to use, and a would-be trainee is told when the cohort starts. The Bridge2AI programme page URL is recorded without a scheme.

sub_elements.name: Related Datasets with Typed Relationships
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: Same shared condition as above, evidenced by E2 distribution_formats and third_party_sharing
sub_elements.evidence: No related_datasets. description and purposes state that CHoRUS is 'one of the four data generation projects' of the Bridge2AI programme and external_resources links the Bridge2AI CHoRUS programme page, but no dataset is named and no relationship is typed
sub_elements.quality_note: CHoRUS sits in a four-project consortium and the record says so twice in prose, yet not one sibling dataset is identified and no relationship such as supplements, derives from or is version of is expressed. The instances decomposition gives internal structure but says nothing about how this dataset relates to anything outside it.

strengths: Source reconciliation is explicit and disciplined. instances[0].source_caveats and the top-level source_caveats name the 50,000 versus 45,000 admission divergence between the project documentation and the September 2025 webinar, state which source was ranked higher and why the lower figure is retained anyway, separate project-level from dataset-level statements in the bundle, and enumerate exactly what the bundle does not contain. Refusing to assert what the sources cannot support is rarer and more valuable than the assertions themselves.

Released and anticipated are held apart everywhere: 50,000 admissions released against 100,000 anticipated across nine modalities, imaging de-identification in process, EEG extraction in process, and the holdout test set recorded under splits as provisioned rather than as a partition already in the data. A reuser is never left to infer which figure describes data they can obtain.

The technical pipeline is complete and traceable. All four halves of the preprocessing sub-element are populated, from OMOP standardization through OHNLP tokenization, waveform conversion and DeGauss geocoding, with cleaning documented as a real feedback loop of characterization reports returned to sites, labeling described, and annotation tooling recorded separately with its output schema. Every step names the repository or protocol that implements it.

Provenance runs end to end for every modality. raw_data_sources traces each content type from its originating clinical system through its pre-transformation format to its access condition, and acquisition_methods separates directly extracted from derived content with the correct provenance flag.

Funding documentation is complete and passes format validation: OT2OD032701 with project number 1OT2OD032701-01, application ID 10472824, the fiscal-year award amount, the awardee institution, the 2022-09-01 to 2026-11-30 project period and a resolvable RePORTER URL, on a correctly formed NIH Other Transaction mechanism with the Common Fund institute code.

The licence distinction is handled correctly. MIT and Apache-2.0 are scoped to the chorus-ai software repositories with an explicit statement that they govern software rather than the dataset, while the clinical data are governed by a separate signed agreement. A record that read the GitHub licence as the dataset licence would have been materially wrong about reuse rights.

Inference is labelled wherever it occurs. The creators, data_governance, collection_timeframes, license_and_use_terms and ethical_reviews blocks each carry a source_caveats stating what the sources actually said and what was reconstructed, including that the recorded collection dates are the award period rather than the clinical encounter range and that the accountable organization is the awardee institution rather than a named accountable body.

Standards conformance is consistent across three levels, the per-modality data standards, the metadata schema and class the record declares for itself, and the standards repeated in distribution_formats and the instances notes, with no drift between them.
weaknesses: The human subjects determination is missing entirely. human_subject_research is unpopulated for a dataset of patient-level ICU, PICU and NICU records, and while the source_caveats discloses that no source makes the determination, the reader is left with no finding either way for identifiable clinical data from 14 hospitals.

There is no consent field at all and no waiver in its place. direct_collection explains why prospective consent does not apply but nothing records a waiver of consent, a HIPAA authorization waiver, an opt-out route or a withdrawal mechanism, so the legal basis for secondary use is absent from the record.

at_risk_populations is empty while the record's own composition slots name pediatric and neonatal intensive care admissions. The vulnerable groups are identified in instances and subpopulations and then omitted from the slot that exists to carry them, which is a documentation choice rather than a source limitation.

Ethics oversight is undocumented and the one structured claim overreaches. No IRB of record, no approval or waiver, no protocol number and no data protection impact assessment appears, and reviewing_organization names the project's own ethics pillar as a reviewer that the entry's own caveat disclaims.

No re-identification risk assessment exists, in a record that volunteers the exposure. participant_privacy discloses that modalities are linked at admission level across 14 hospitals and that OMOP Location entities are geocoded, then gives no residual risk level, determination, method or responsible party.

Bias is described but never categorized. known_biases is absent; the representativeness finding sits under known_limitations with no enumerated bias type, so nothing is machine-readable as bias documentation and measurement and representation bias go unregistered.

No persistent identifier and no version. id is a fragment on the project homepage, there is no DOI, RRID, accession or citation, and no version, version_access or errata for a dataset the record itself describes as a partial release still growing, so an analysis cannot be pinned to what it read.

The cohort is never characterized. Care setting and contributing hospital are given, but no age, sex, race, ethnicity or geographic distribution, no inclusion or exclusion criteria and no per-setting counts against the 50,000 admissions, so a reuser cannot judge who is in the data.

No variable-level metadata exists and the one structural flag is questionable. 1.6 billion rows are reported with no statement of what a row contains, no column or concept is defined for any modality, and is_tabular is set to false even though the OMOP portion is tabular by construction.

No anomalies are documented. Source disagreement and coverage gaps are recorded, but no outliers, artefacts, sensor dropouts or cross-site OMOP coding inconsistencies, which is a conspicuous silence given that the record documents a characterization-report process whose findings would populate exactly this slot.
